scope: STM32H743VIT6 LQFP100, WeAct V1.2 P1/P2/P3 headers, and every application-configured GPIO/oscillator at the pinned firmware baseline. MCU capabilities, board wiring and firmware assignments are separate datasets joined by GPIO.
v0_default: Pending corrected V0 routing; no net assignment established by this audit.

v0_by_gpio.PC8: Pending V0 pin choice; current PWM shares microSD D0.

bench_evidence.observation: First module revision 1.2 read under LCD immediately right of ribbon slot.

The guided bench review verified selected segments on Board A and normal heartbeat/reset observations on the tested module. Other contact segments and fitted component identities/values remain drawing evidence or unverified; the per-record observations define the scope.
Owner identifies both modules as WeAct V1.2. The first module marking was directly read under the LCD; no independent revision check was performed by this audit.

Earlier visual inspection: SB3 alone appeared closed on both owner-identified V1.2 modules; SB1, SB2, SB4, SB5 and SB6 appeared open. The later guided review electrically confirmed SB3 on Board A only; fitted part identity/value remains unverified.
F1 protection remains uncorrected on physical carrier and design.

Earlier handbrake PWM activity and a Web Config handbrake command registering in the Fanatec Windows application were owner-reported functional observations. The command route and coverage of dedicated handbrake-port configurations remain unspecified.

Physical reset-button and software reboot captures were made at external P2:10 (NR). The reboot waveform stayed near zero for approximately 26 µs at that contact; internal reset duration, dfu and downstream TFT/camera reset lines were not measured.

bench_review.source_comparison_result: Verified from Git: the three intervening commits changed only simhub-plugin/Directory.Build.props and simhub-plugin/src/Fanadapter.Core/PortLocator.cs. Audited firmware files are identical.
bench_review.conditions: Owner-guided review, primarily a bare WeAct Mini STM32H743VIT6 V1.2 module connected to macOS over USB-C; Rigol MHO984 oscilloscope and Fluke 115 multimeter. Board A/B identities are stated where recorded. Reset/heartbeat module A/B identity and the power/isolation state for individual resistance readings were not specified in the report.
bench_review.evidence_limits: Contact and connection observations below verify only their named segments or normal operating behavior. Scope acquisition/cursors were saved on the Rigol; raw export is unconfirmed. Resistance readings are reported as measured, not converted into fitted component values.
bench_review.earlier_functional_observations: Earlier owner reports of H-pattern/sequential shifting, pedal UART operation, handbrake PWM activity and a Web Config handbrake command seen in the Fanatec Windows application are separate functional evidence. They do not establish which handbrake path carried that command or complete dedicated-port coverage.
bench_review.disposition: Routine bench review is complete for this mapping audit. Remaining drawing-only segments and inconclusive readings are limits on evidence, not a requirement to test every pin. Future pin allocation and assembly-label changes are separate work.
